# Mahāhaṁsajātaka (Ja 534)

**ID:** Ja 534  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mahāhaṁsajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0514m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0514m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāhaṁsajātaka* (Ja 534) is a birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon, titled in English as *The Longer Tale of the Golden Goose*. Set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) in Rājagaha, the introductory frame concerns the Elder Ānanda's willingness to sacrifice his life for the Buddha [Fausböll 1891]. The story opens with the verse incipit *Ete haṁsā pakkamanti* ("There go the birds") [Fausböll 1891].

In an extended dialogue with the king, the goose expounds the ten royal virtues (*dasa-rājadhamma*): generosity (*dāna*), morality (*sīla*), self-sacrifice (*pariccāga*), uprightness (*ajjava*), gentleness (*maddava*), austerity (*tapa*), non-anger (*akkodha*), non-violence (*avihiṁsa*), forbearance (*khanti*), and non-obstruction (*avirodhana*) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Thich Nhat Tu and Thich Duc Thien 2019; Tambiah]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the king is identified as Sāriputta, Queen Khemā as the nun Khemā, Sumukha as Ānanda, the hunter as Channa, and the goose king Dhataraṭṭha as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1891].
